DESCRIPTION: Failure classification and evidence ingestion are disconnected. `process_round()` records failures from `responses`, but it always feeds the original `findings` list into convergence, diminishing-returns, and fingerprint updates without filtering out findings from responses already classified as `EMPTY`, `TIMEOUT`, `MALFORMED`, or `FORMAT`. I reproduced a `parseable=False` response that returned `FailureType.MALFORMED`; the same round still stored one finding in `ConvergenceDetector._round_findings[0]` and counted one novel class. Invalid evidence can therefore advance convergence, inflate yield, and steer future routing.  
PROPOSED_FIX: After failure detection, derive an accepted-response set and discard findings from failed responses before calling Areas 4/5 or `update_fingerprints()`.

DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer` accepts an empty model pool and returns a successful-looking result instead of failing fast. I reproduced `LoadBalancer([], [Task("t1", ...)], {}, cfg).solve()` returning an allocation with shape `(1, 0)`, `row_sum=0`, `cost=0.0`, and `balanced=True`, with only a warning for the unassigned task. That turns an impossible dispatch into a normal return value that downstream code could easily treat as valid.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reject `models=[]` in `__init__()` or `solve()`, or return an explicit infeasible-result type rather than `(Allocation, cost, balanced)`.

DESCRIPTION: Recovery escalation is based on lifetime same-type counts, not retry-like recurrence. `get_recovery()` counts all historical failures of the same type and never resets or decays that count after healthy rounds. I reproduced `TIMEOUT` recoveries at rounds `0`, `10`, and `20` yielding `RETRY_EXTENDED`, `RETRY_EXTENDED`, then `EXCLUDE`. The long healthy gap does not matter; sparse failures eventually eject the model anyway. That is much harsher than the documented “after retry” semantics.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Escalate on consecutive same-type failures or a bounded recent window, and reset/decay the counter after successful responses.

DESCRIPTION: Several public accessors leak live mutable internal state. `ConvergenceDetector.get_round_classes()` and `get_cumulative_classes()` return cached list objects directly, and `DynamicManager.round_results` returns the live mutable `RoundResult` instances. I reproduced `cd.get_round_classes(0).clear()` permanently emptying the cached class list, and `mgr.round_results[0].converged = True` plus `mgr.round_results[0].active_models.clear()` mutating `mgr._round_results[0]` in place. External code can silently rewrite audit history and convergence state without any validation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Return immutable or copied structures from public getters, and make `RoundResult`/equivalence-class containers frozen or copy-on-read.
